full_judgment:
6. Both the trial Court and the High Court Division on appeal concurrently found that the plaintiff-respondent is a financial institution and that the suit is maintainable in the Artha Rin Adalat. The High Court Division in particular found that the aforesaid transaction was made upon instructions of the plaintiff-respondent and that defendant Nos. 2 and 3-petitioners are liable to pay the claimed amount to the plaintiff-respondent. The High Court Division further held that since the petitioners did not file the appeal in the High Court Division on depositing 50% of the decrial amount, the appeal is barred by limitation. 

 9. We find that the appeal was filed within time. So, it cannot be said to be barred by limitation, but reading section 7 of the Act as a whole we find that there are three stages in the filing of the appeal. First, the party who lost in the Artha Rin Adalat must form an intention to file an appeal. Secondly, that party must deposit 50% of the decrial costs in the High Court Division and thirdly, the party must file the appeal within the period of special limitation of 30 days provided in section 7(1) of the Act. This is a special statute and is governed by the language of the statute itself. The decision of the Indian Supreme Court is no guide to its interpretation. The entertainment of the appeal at the filing stage is the point of time when it is to be seen whether the required deposit has been made or not.
